content.title: When and Where Will Artemis II's Orion Capsule Land After Its Moon Mission?
content.text: Now that the four astronauts of the Artemis II mission officially made it farther from Earth than any other humans, those keeping up with the latest news surrounding their historic journey may be wondering what's next.The astronauts' journey marks the first manned moon mission in more than five decades, since the Apollo 17 spaceflight in December of 1972.And we have all the details on when and where the Artemis II crew is set to touch down.RELATED: NBC News' Tom Costello Compares the Artemis II Mission to the Back To the Future MovieThe Artemis II "is scheduled to splash down off the coast of San Diego at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT on Friday, April 10," according to NASA.The United States Navy will be on-site in San Diego, California, to offer a helping hand, with the USS John P. Murtha standing by to recover the Artemis II astronauts after their return to Earth, according to City News Service. And a Navy helicopter will help track the Orion space capsule as it re-enters the Earth's atmosphere. How the Artemis II astronauts made history on April 6, 2026April 6 was a momentous day as the Artemis II team set the record for the farthest distance a human has ever traveled away from Earth.RELATED: All the Shows NBC Has Renewed in 2026"The momentous day began at 1:56 p.m. EDT as NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen, set the record for the farthest distance from Earth traveled by any human, surpassing Apollo 13’s distance of 248,655 miles," NASA shared. "During a planned 40-minute loss of signal as Orion passed behind the moon, the spacecraft and its crew made their closest approach at 7 p.m., flying at about 4,067 miles above the surface. Two minutes later, the crew reached the mission’s maximum distance from Earth at 252,756 miles, setting a new record for human spaceflight."How to watch Artemis II's return to EarthTo see Artemis II return to Earth on Friday, April 10, stay tuned to NASA's YouTube channel as well as NBC News NOW for the latest. NBC News NOW is NBC's free, 24/7 streaming news channel that can be accessed via NBCNews.com/now, the NBC News smartphone app, YouTube, Peacock, and other streaming platforms.With the splashdown in the Pacific Ocean scheduled for approximately 8:07 p.m. ET, it's best to tune in before the official return time for updates.
